climate_pressure: The 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods.
fcv_mediator: Inadequate shelter divisions, privacy and security, as described by the rights mission.
possible_consequence: Reports of sexual and gender-based violence in shelters, including Porto Alegre; not a measured population-wide increase.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing gender inequality and violence, shelter arrangements and reporting access also affect harm and recorded cases.
uncertainty: Mission-reported cases and risk mechanisms, not prevalence, a counterfactual causal estimate or anthropogenic event attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The mission recommended protection protocols and documented women-and-children-only shelters; coverage and effectiveness were not evaluated.
compact_statement: Flood displacement into inadequately protected shelters was associated with reported sexual and gender-based violence in the 2024 response.

climate_pressure: Amazon drought and low river levels.
documented_impact: River-dependent communities face isolation and reduced access to services and assistance.
fcv_mediator: Armed-group resource exploitation, recruitment and forced displacement compound access restrictions in drought-affected areas.
possible_consequence: Greater difficulty reaching already isolated communities and heightened protection needs.
alternative_explanations: Remoteness, transport infrastructure, service coverage and enforcement limitations also shape access.
uncertainty: ACAPS secondary qualitative synthesis; armed-group citations were not independently rechecked. No claim that drought created armed groups or that a quantified interaction effect was estimated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Reported food, water and medical distribution offers a response channel; effectiveness and safe coverage were not evaluated.
compact_statement: ACAPS describes insecurity compounding drought-related isolation and humanitarian access constraints, not drought causing armed conflict.
